title: A serving is not a portion
standfirst: The panel describes a serving. You decide the portion. They are rarely the same.

spans.text: Every number on a panel hangs off one line near the top: the serving size. Miss that line and the rest of the panel means something other than what you read.
A serving is not advice. It is a reference amount, set so the same food from different brands can be compared fairly.
They are meant to match what people really eat at once. Several were raised for that reason, which made some numbers look worse overnight, though the food had not changed.
The panel says a serving. The pack holds a portion. If a bottle holds more than one serving, each number has to be multiplied before it describes what you drank.
This is the most common way a label is misread. It is not carelessness. The sums are fiddly and the pack is not built to help.
Find the serving size. Then find how many servings the pack holds. If they differ, the panel describes only part of what you are holding.

blocks.cue: When I pick up a bottle or a bag
blocks.action: I will check how many servings it holds before I read the rest
